section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the verse "You are standing today, all of you" refers to Rosh Hashanah, the Day of Judgment, and that standing signifies being vindicated in judgment.
section.t: "You are standing today, all of you, before Hashem your G-d: your heads, your tribes, etc., from the hewer of your wood to the drawer of your water."
Now, this portion
is always read before Rosh Hashanah.
And it is hinted in the word "today" that it refers to Rosh Hashanah,
as it is stated
by our teacher who received from his teacher the Maggid, and his teacher from his teacher the Baal Shem Tov, that "today" refers to Rosh Hashanah,
which is the Day of Judgment,
and as it is stated,
"And it was the day,"
and the Targum translates: "And it was the great Day of Judgment,"
for Rosh Hashanah is the day of judgment and justice,
and this is the blessing: "You are standing today, all of you,"
that you, all of you, from your heads, your tribes, to the hewer of your wood and the drawer of your water,
are standing, enduring and existing,
meaning that they are vindicated in judgment.
